newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close again at 1996 high.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close again at 1996 high.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks soared ahead in Monday trade, with the Hang Seng index jumping to a new 1996 high on an improved outlook for interest rates and upward revisions in corporate earnings forecasts, brokers said.
"We are getting positive economic signals and stronger than expected corporate earnings, said Amy Wong, research director at New China Hong Kong Securities Ltd.
The Hang Seng index put on 143.04 points to close at 11,906.43, following through on its 123-point rise on Friday. The index hit a session high of 11,906.02.
Monday's close was the highest since February 4, 1994 when the index closed at 12,157.57.
Turnover was an active HK$5.96 billion, just higher than Friday's HK$5.82 billion.
The index has advanced 280.30 points, or 2.4 percent points, in the last five trading sessions.
"We are revising upwards our corporate earnings forecast for 1996 to about an average 16 percent to 17 percent. I think that most of the houses are the same (revising up)," said Wong.
The property sector led the market most of the day, with a gain of 1.91 percent to 22,379.68 for the properties sub-index, compared with the Hang Seng's 1.22 percent gain.
Besides properties, investors sought market laggards -- utilities were the next best blue chip performers and the Hang Seng China Enterprise Index advanced a massive 3.71 percent.
"We saw some chasing of laggards and property stocks, Cheung Kong in particular," said Peter Lai, associate director of OCBC Securities.
Cheung Kong, the most actively traded issue on Monday, added HK$2.00 to HK$59.50 after touching an intra-day record at HK$59.75.
Sun Hung Kai Properties also rose to a record high, putting on HK$1.50 to close at HK$82.25. The company will report earnings for the year ended June 30 on Wednesday.
Henderson Land regained upward momentum, adding HK$1.25 to HK$66.25, just below its high of HK$66.50.
In the utility sector, China Light continued its rapid catch up, putting on HK$0.40 to HK$36.00, while Hongkong Electric eased HK$0.05. Its interim dividend is payable on October 2.
In the H share sector, Beiren Printing added HK$0.06 to HK$1.58, and Zhenhai Refining put on HK$0.05 to HK$2.10.
